name: Cool Graph
description: You are given an undirected graph with $$$n$$$ vertices and $$$m$$$ edges. You can perform the following operation at most $$$2\cdot \max(n,m)$$$ times: Choose three distinct vertices $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$, and $$$c$$$, then for each of the edges $$$(a,b)$$$, $$$(b,c)$$$, and $$$(c,a)$$$, do the following: If the edge does not exist, add it. On the contrary, if it exists, remove it. A graph is called cool if and only if one of the following holds: The graph has no edges, or The graph is a tree. You have to make the graph cool by performing the above operations. Note that you can use at most $$$2\cdot \max(n,m)$$$ operations. It can be shown that there always exists at least one solution.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1\le t\le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$3\le n\le 10^5$$$, $$$0\le m\le \min\left(\frac{n(n-1)}{2},2\cdot 10^5\right)$$$) — the number of vertices and the number of edges. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, the $$$i$$$-th line contains two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ ($$$1\le u_i,v_i\le n$$$) — the two nodes that the $$$i$$$-th edge connects. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$, and the sum of $$$m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2\cdot 10^5$$$. It is guaranteed that there are no self-loops or multiple-edges in the given graph.
output_specification: For each test case, in the first line output an integer $$$k$$$ ($$$0\le k\le 2\cdot \max(n, m)$$$) — the number of operations. Then output $$$k$$$ lines, the $$$i$$$-th line containing three distinct integers $$$a$$$, $$$b$$$, and $$$c$$$ ($$$1\le a,b,c\le n$$$) — the three integers you choose in the $$$i$$$-th operation. If there are multiple solutions, you can output any of them.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2029D — Cool Graph [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
